To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Polyakov loop correlation function is given by the one-loop free energy of the bosonic string, that this free energy is the sum of contributions from topologically inequivalent sectors of the cylinder in bosonic string target space, that the contribution from the sector that winds once around the cylinder reproduces exactly the free energy of the Nambu--Goto model, that in the sector that winds twice around the cylinder the string world-sheet is a cylinder with a twist, and that in the sector

(1) the Polyakov loop is a closed string operator, (2) the Polyakov correlator in d = 10 is the partition function of a single D0-D0 string, and (3) the Polyakov free energy in d = 2 is the free energy of a single D1-D1 string.

(1) Polyakov loop correlators can be derived in a consistent way from the free boson theory of strings, (2) the one-loop result is consistent with the Nambu–Goto result only if the world-sheet d = 26 and the Liouville field is taken into account, and (3) the result is in agreement with the Montecarlo data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction of D0-branes in the bosonic string.
the study of the effective action describing the dynamics of a single D0-brane.
the computation of the free energy of a system consisting of two parallel D0-branes separated by a distance R in bosonic string.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for large R, the Polyakov loop free energy is given by the one-loop Nambu-Guto partition function, and at shorter scales it is not known.
the Polyakov loop correlation functions in bosonic string are well understood at long distances, while at short distances they are not.

the Polyakov loop correlation function in bosonic string is given by the Nambu-Go- to expression, plus a correction that is exponentially small in R and that can be interpreted in terms of closed string exchange.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a consistent bosonic string theory, the Polyakov loop has the expected properties of a confining potential.
the Polyakov loop correlation function in the Nambu Goto theory is reproduced in a covariant quantized theory, but only at the level of the one loop free energy.
the free energy of Polyakov loops is a non-trivial function of R and of the string coupling constant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Polyakov loop correlation function in the Nambu- Goto theory is a non-trivial result of the worldsheet duality, and not of the specific choice of the boundary condition.
the Polyakov loop is a well defined operator on the worldsheet, which can be used to probe the dynamics of the theory.
the Polyakov loop is a non-local object that cannot be defined in terms of local operators, but only in terms of open strings attached to the D-branes.
